reviewer.verbatimPublicReport:
## Batch027 independent read-only review

**C1: CLEAN. C2: CLEAN. C3: CLEAN — within the bounded scope described below. No actionable findings or required corrections established.**

This was one whole-rubric review. I did not edit content, run tests, delegate, launch agents/workflows, or inspect the ordinary English/app checkouts.

### Snapshot and preservation

- **RU:** `6754635bb376e92d5176e7e906e8e23b66599b56`
- **Branch:** `full-ru-027-numeral-words`
- **Signature:** Git reported `G`.
- **Frozen EN:** `6af98cb717755690a9ca793e5454a96ebd7a8f9f`

Both HEADs remained unchanged. RU tracked files remained clean; the only status entry was the pre-existing untracked `tools\__pycache__\`. The frozen EN worktree remained clean.

Final fingerprint inspection found:
- All **795 runtime paths** matched their manifest fingerprints in the appropriate text/binary byte domains.
- All **14 new working-RAW fingerprints** matched the candidate.
- The manifest’s working-RAW hash matched the author’s receipt.
- The baseline-to-candidate runtime diff contained only the 14 new word files, with no modifications to baseline runtime files.

These were read-only inspections, not validator or test execution. Working RAW, canonical Git RAW and normalized LF were not treated as universally identical.

## Actual independent reading

### Complete articles: 39 EN/RU pairs

I read every complete source and Russian body, including all 25 unchanged context pairs—not merely their titles or metadata.

New words: ゼロ、一、七、万、三、九、二、五、八、六、千、四、百、零.

Baseline context:
- Twelve kanji cards: 一、七、万、三、九、二、五、八、六、千、四、百.
- Thirteen word articles: 一つ、七つ、三つ、三千、三百、九つ、二つ、五つ、八つ、六つ、六百、十、四つ.

Successful pair ranges were:

`[0,2), [2,4), [4,6), [6,8), [8,10), [10,12), [12,14), [14,16), [16,18), [18,20), [20,22), [22,24), [24,26), [26,28), [28,30), [30,32), [32,34), [34,36), [36,38), [38,39)`.

### Answer pool: 483 metadata/title/guard rows

I read all 483 actual combined Russian rows and considered displayed meanings in both quiz directions. This was **not a reading of 483 complete bodies**.

Successful pool ranges:

`[0,35), [35,70), [70,105), [105,140), [140,175), [175,210), [210,245), [245,280), [280,315), [315,350), [350,385), [385,420), [420,455), [455,483)`.

### Lexical evidence: 14 complete selected objects

Successful lexical ranges:

`[0,2), [2,5), [5,8), [8,11), [11,14)`.

I read the complete selected objects, including forms, readings, senses, restrictions and qualifiers. These were captured source objects, not fresh API requests or a claim to have read every unrelated result in each raw response. Their capture fingerprints matched the adjudication record.

All required reader outputs completed below the **18,000-UTF8-byte refusal threshold**, with explicit completion markers. No refused reader call was counted as reading.

I also read the required active/scoped instructions, all three rubrics, methodology and format reference, source-adjudication and authoring-freeze records, relevant frozen format/confusable guidance, and the frozen vocabulary policy and 17 source rows mapping to these 14 articles. Author reading receipts were not substituted for independent reading.

## C1 — Japanese correctness: CLEAN within scope

The translations preserve the numerical meanings, Japanese examples and readings without introducing an established consequential error.

Particular checks included:

- **四 and 七:** native primary readings よん／なな remain distinguished from Sino-Japanese し／しち.
- **九:** both きゅう and く are taught with fixed-use examples, not unrestricted interchangeability.
- **万:** four-digit grouping, multipliers and the distinction between numbers and 円／人 units remain correct.
- Sound changes and special readings remain correctly represented:  
  一個いっこ、一分いっぷん、七月しちがつ、七日なのか、三本さんぼん、三日みっか、九時くじ、九月くがつ、二人ふたり、二日ふつか、五日いつか、五月ごがつ、八日ようか、八分はっぷん、六日むいか、六本ろっぽん、六百ろっぴゃく、三千さんぜん、八千はっせん、四人よにん、四時よじ、四日よっか、三百さんびゃく、八百はっぴゃく.
- Full sentence translations preserve the relevant quantities, participants, actions and negation.
- 零点五／れいてんご remains unchanged; Russian **0,5** is appropriate.

Important source qualifications were respected:

- The ゼロ query had **zero literal ゼロ spelling matches**. The selected object actually lists ０／〇／零 read ゼロ, with a kana-only-use note in another sense. This supports the documented variant evidence, not literal-spelling-match proof.
- 百’s separate **Place “Hyaku”** sense was not used as numeral evidence.
- 万’s よろず-restricted “everything/various” senses were not transferred to numeric まん.
- API JLPT differences, including 九’s N3 result, do not override the frozen community N5 vocabulary policy.
- Frozen numeric JMdict IDs remain attribution; they were **not independently API-ID-verified**.

No consequential new Japanese teaching claim remains unresolved in this review. This does not constitute fresh specialist certification of every inherited historical, etymological or frequency claim in the baseline context.

## C2 — Consistency, dependencies and quiz guards: CLEAN within scope

The fourteen articles retain their Japanese IDs, readings, types, levels, canonical tags and teaching content. Required localized headings and source attribution are consistent.

Actual new-word link destinations exist where cards are available. For `words\零.md`, removing only the unavailable link wrapper is correct: 零 and `kanji: [零]` remain intact. 八百 and 八千 correctly remain unlinked teaching expressions; absent word files do not require fabricated placeholders.

### All ten direct exclusions

| Pair | Decision |
|---|---|
| 一–一つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| 二–二つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| 三–三つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| 四–四つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| 五–五つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| 六–六つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| 七–七つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| 八–八つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| 九–九つ | Valid conservative same-quantity safeguard; retain. |
| ゼロ–零 | Valid direct semantic safeguard; retain. Both titles are «ноль». |

The first nine are justified by the actual generic-count bodies and overlapping bare quantities. Their differently worded Russian titles alone do not establish safe opposing answers. They are conservative editorial choices, not a claim that this is the uniquely mandatory guard policy.

For ゼロ–零, exact-title deduplication already provides protection under the documented builder; the explicit exclusion is therefore defensively redundant there, but semantically valid.

One-sided declarations correctly represent direct symmetric pairs. No mirrored declarations or transitive expansion are needed. I found **no additional missing direct same-meaning guard involving the batch** in the inspected pool. Dates, months, people and currency units retain material meanings; shared digits do not justify cliques.

## C3 — Russian comprehensibility: CLEAN within scope

The learner-facing text is understandable without English. Numerical contrasts, irregular readings and examples are explained coherently across the family.

The adaptations in 六 and 千 replace English-dependent comparisons with useful Japanese noun-number, counter and unit explanations without deleting the teaching rule. Russian sentence glosses preserve the intended lessons. No wording issue was established that requires correction; optional polish is not being promoted into a finding.

## Validation attribution and remaining boundaries

I read the author’s validation receipt: manifest **795**, version `d449a612af670113`, validator **0 errors**, **124 tests OK** in **30.360s**, and budget **803 files / 812 entries / 2,294,558 retained bytes / 2,311,240 inflated bytes / 1,148,688 ZIP bytes**. **I did not rerun these commands or claim them as my own testing.**

The app’s Russian display mapping for canonical tag `quantity` remains **UNVERIFIED**, not an established missing mapping or content defect.

No acceptance/tracking records were changed. This report does not authorize activation, release, device use, playback, new audio/media generation, C6/C7 approval, native-human certification or whole-corpus acceptance.
